'''John William Boldeman''' is an Australian nuclear scientist and winner of many scientific awards and medals, including an [[Australian and New Zealand Association for the Advancement of Science|ANZAAS Medal]] in 2007,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.anzaas.org.au/press/Boldeman_ANZAAS.pdf |title=Archived copy |access-date=18 April 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110226025801/http://anzaas.org.au/press/Boldeman_ANZAAS.pdf |archive-date=26 February 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref> the Clunies Ross Lifetime Achievement Award,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.probonoaustralia.com.au/news/2010/05/australia%E2%80%99s-visionary-innovators-honoured|title = Australia's Visionary Innovators Honoured}}</ref> as well as an being officer of the order of Australia. He was born in [[Longreach]], [[Queensland]], the eldest of seven children born to Harold and Eileen Boldeman.  He spent much of his childhood in [[Maryborough, Queensland]] and attended the Maryborough Christian Brothers High School and then [[Nudgee College]] in [[Brisbane]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.frasercoastchronicle.com.au/news/old-boys-do-us-proud-john-boldeman-andrew-jesset/543304/ |newspaper=Fraser Coast Chronicle |date=28 May 2010 |first=Loretta |last=Bryce |title='Old boys' do us proud |accessdate=31 January 2017 |url-status=live |archivedate=31 January 2017 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170131015627/http://www.frasercoastchronicle.com.au/news/old-boys-do-us-proud-john-boldeman-andrew-jesset/543304/ }}</ref> He went on to study physics at the [[University of Queensland]] and joined the then Australian Atomic Energy Commission on graduation, continuing his studies in association with his work. Boldeman worked at the AAEC, and then [[ANSTO]], for 42 years, rising to the position of Director of Physics. He was awarded a PhD from [[Wollongong University]], and a D.Sc. from [[University of New South Wales]] in 1984. He organised the purchase and installation of the Antares accelerator in 1988 at ANSTO.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ansto.gov.au/AboutANSTO/MediaCentre/News/ACS069657 |title=Two ANSTO scientists made an Officer of the Order of Australia &#124; ANSTO |website=www.ansto.gov.au |access-date=February 14, 2016}}</ref>

Boldeman is best known for his contribution to the [[Australian Synchrotron]] located near [[Monash University]] in [[Melbourne]]. Heavily involved in the development of the project from initiation in the 90's, Boldeman became the Foundation Technical Director in 2001, and also principal advisor to the Victorian government for the Synchrotron.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.ansto.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0007/46591/Final_Boldeman-V2.pdf |title=Archived copy |access-date=18 April 2011 |archive-date=29 March 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110329052359/http://www.ansto.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0007/46591/Final_Boldeman-V2.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> He co-designed and monitored the construction of the Australian Synchrotron. This included design of the lattice structure.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.abc.net.au/ra/innovations/stories/s2901365.htm|title=ABC Radio Australia|website=[[Australian Broadcasting Corporation]]}}</ref>

Boldeman received a lifetime contribution award for his work on the ANTARES Tandem Accelerator and the [[Australian Synchrotron]].<ref>{{cite news | first = Loretta | last = Bryce | title = 'Old boys' do us proud | date = 2010-05-28 | publisher = APN News & Media Ltd 2010. | url = http://www.frasercoastchronicle.com.au/story/2010/05/28/old-boys-do-us-proud-john-boldeman-andrew-jesset/ | work = Fraser Coast Chronicle | accessdate = 2010-05-29}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.synchrotron.org.au/index.php/about-us/history/australian-synchrotron-research-program|title=Search results &#124; ANSTO}}</ref>

Boldeman was elected a fellow of the [[Australian Academy of Technological Sciences and Engineering|Australian Academy of Technological Science and Engineering]] in 1993. He was made an Officer of the General Division of the [[Order of Australia]] in 2015 for services to Australian Science and Technology.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nuclearaustralia.org.au/prof-barry-allen-ao-and-prof-john-boldeman-ao/ |title=Professor Barry Allen AO and Professor John Boldeman AO – Australian Nuclear Association |access-date=2 February 2016 |archive-date=29 February 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160229114308/http://www.nuclearaustralia.org.au/prof-barry-allen-ao-and-prof-john-boldeman-ao/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

He is also co-founder and current vice-president of Gunnamatta youth weight training association in South [[Cronulla]].
